frames.narration: Deploy: the new checkout page ships to production behind the flag new-checkout, which is off. Code is deployed but nobody sees it.
Release step one: the engineer sets the rollout to 10% in the flag service. No deploy is needed.
user-1 opens checkout. The SDK evaluates locally: hash of new-checkout:v1:user-1 gives bucket 3186, which is not below 1000, so user-1 gets the old page.
Error rates for the 10% group look healthy, so the engineer raises the rollout to 50%. The rule is pushed to the app.
user-1 reloads. Same hash, same bucket 3186, and now it is below 5000, so user-1 gets the new page. Anyone who was already inside the 10% still is: raising the percentage only adds users.
Errors on the new page spike. The engineer flips the kill switch; the flag goes off for everyone within seconds, with no rollback and no deploy.
Later the flag service becomes unreachable. The app does not call it per request: it keeps its last known rules. A flag it had never loaded would fall back to the safe default in code, which is off.
Fixed and released to 100% a week later, the flag has done its job. The team deletes the flag, the if and the old page, so no stale flag is left to confuse the next engineer.
